items.new: Of the Right Whale, the best outline pictures are in Scoresby. But they are drawn on too small a scale to give the impression one would want. He has only one picture of whaling scenes, and this is a sad deficiency, because it is only through such pictures, when done even reasonably well, that you can get anything like a truthful idea of the living whale as seen by his living hunters.

items.new: But though, to landsmen in general, the native inhabitants of the seas have always been regarded with feelings unspeakably unsociable and repellent; though we know the sea to be an everlasting terra incognita, so that Columbus sailed over numberless unknown worlds to discover his one superficial western one; though by far the most terrible of all mortal disasters have, from time immemorial and without distinction, befallen tens and hundreds of thousands of those who have gone upon the waters; though only a moment's consideration will teach that, however much baby man may brag of his science and skill, and however much, in a flattering future, that science and skill may increase, yet forever and forever, to the crack of doom, the sea will insult and murder him, and pulverize the stateliest, stiffest frigate he can make — nevertheless, by the continual repetition of these very impressions, man has lost that sense of the full awfulness of the sea which originally belongs to it.

items.new: Whether the fleeting attendance of that one still and solitary jet had gradually worked upon Ahab, so that he was now prepared to connect the ideas of gentleness and calm with the first sight of the particular whale he hunted, or whether his eagerness misled him — whichever way it might have been, no sooner did he clearly perceive the white mass than with a quick intensity he instantly gave orders for lowering.
